thesis_health.reason: The first evidence-based baseline confirms orderly monetary normalization and continued governance reform, while real-income and imported-inflation risks prevent an upgrade to strengthening.

scenarios.description: Orderly monetary normalization, durable wage-price interaction, effective governance reform, and improving real household income broaden market leadership.
entry_conditions: BOJ normalization continues without funding or credit stress.
Governance reform produces measurable capital-allocation improvements.
Market leadership broadens beyond currency-sensitive exporters.
exit_conditions: Equity returns narrow to FX-dependent companies.

scenarios.description: Nominal growth and reform continue, but higher import costs, weak household purchasing power, and policy uncertainty produce uneven outcomes.
entry_conditions: Financial conditions remain accommodative despite higher policy rates.
Consumption remains resilient but does not accelerate materially.
Governance reform advances unevenly across companies.
exit_conditions: Domestic demand broadens enough to support the bull scenario.
Persistent real-income deterioration or financial stress supports the bear scenario.

scenarios.description: Inflation remains externally driven, real income deteriorates, or policy tightening creates funding, credit, or domestic-demand stress.
entry_conditions: JGB volatility or funding stress rises sharply.
Governance reform reverses or fails to affect capital allocation.
exit_conditions: Financial conditions remain stable through additional normalization.
Company-level governance actions produce durable returns.

decision.summary: The JPY thesis is intact and merits targeted deep dives into financial normalization and governance-reform beneficiaries, but incomplete domestic-demand confirmation and imported-inflation risks argue against broad portfolio promotion.
required_actions: Build valuation-ready screens for financial normalization beneficiaries.
Identify companies with completed governance and capital-allocation actions.
Review second-quarter GDP and current real-wage evidence before changing thesis health.
Compare hedged and unhedged Japan exposure.
Do not issue company entry prices or company buy or sell decisions within the theme review.

developments.fact: The Bank of Japan maintained the uncollateralized overnight call-rate target at around 1.0 percent by an 8-1 vote; one member proposed 1.25 percent.
developments.interpretation: Normalization is continuing without evidence of abrupt tightening or current market dysfunction, although the dissent indicates increased upside-policy risk.
developments.action: Maintain financial normalization as the highest-ranked opportunity and monitor BOJ opinions, JGB volatility, funding conditions, and credit quality.

developments.fact: The BOJ projected moderate growth, resilient private consumption, tight labor conditions, continued nominal-wage growth, and weakness in household sentiment.
developments.interpretation: Nominal growth remains supportive, but domestic demand is resilient rather than clearly accelerating.
developments.action: Keep domestic consumption opportunities below financial and governance opportunities until real-income and consumption evidence improves.

developments.fact: The BOJ projected underlying inflation around 2 percent while warning that yen depreciation and commodity costs are increasing import prices and reducing household real income.
developments.interpretation: Inflation durability is improving, but imported inflation can weaken consumption and small-company margins; currency translation alone is not a durable return engine.
developments.action: Prioritize companies with pricing power, productivity gains, or domestic cost advantages and remove FX translation when evaluating exporter quality.

developments.fact: The Tokyo Stock Exchange implemented revised listing regulations associated with the July 2026 Corporate Governance Code revision.
developments.interpretation: The institutional governance-reform framework has advanced, but company-level capital-allocation outcomes remain the required confirmation test.
developments.action: Screen for completed buybacks, cross-shareholding reductions, asset disposals, ROE improvements, and productive reinvestment before promoting named companies.

developments.fact: Japan's first-quarter 2026 real GDP increased 0.5 percent quarter over quarter, with a positive domestic-demand contribution and moderate household-consumption growth.
developments.interpretation: The economy remains outside a renewed-deflationary contraction regime, but the data do not yet establish a broad consumption-led expansion.
developments.action: Use the August 17 second-quarter GDP release as the next major test of domestic-demand breadth.

scorecard.reason: Moderate economic growth, positive first-quarter GDP, continued nominal-wage growth, and a durable wage-price mechanism support the assumption.
The BOJ maintained a 1.0 percent policy setting while reporting accommodative financial conditions and no current funding or credit stress.
The revised governance code and listing rules strengthen the institutional framework, but company-level implementation remains uneven and unverified.
Consumption is resilient and wages are rising, but household sentiment and real-income pressure prevent full confirmation.
Weak-yen translation can support reported profits while also raising input costs; company-level margin, unit, and pricing evidence is required.

assumptions_changed.reason: The initial baseline finds continuing nominal growth and a durable wage-price mechanism.
Policy normalization has advanced while financial conditions remain accommodative.
The July 2026 governance-code and listing-rule revisions strengthen the institutional reform framework.
Consumption resilience is offset by weak household sentiment and imported-inflation pressure on real income.
Theme-level evidence cannot distinguish exporter pricing power from currency translation.

catalysts.name: BOJ policy normalization
catalysts.confirmation_test: Additional normalization occurs without sharp JGB volatility, funding stress, credit deterioration, or a material domestic-demand slowdown.
catalysts.failure_test: A disorderly yield move, tightening financial conditions, or policy tightening into weakening demand.

catalysts.name: Wage and real-income transmission
catalysts.confirmation_test: Nominal wages exceed consumer-price growth durably and household consumption strengthens.
catalysts.failure_test: Persistent real-wage deterioration and declining household consumption.

catalysts.name: Governance reform
catalysts.confirmation_test: Listed companies execute capital returns, reduce cross-shareholdings, improve asset efficiency, and raise productive investment.
catalysts.failure_test: Compliance disclosures increase without measurable balance-sheet or operating changes.

catalysts.name: Yen regime shift
catalysts.confirmation_test: Currency stabilization reduces imported inflation without damaging exporter competitiveness or financial conditions.
catalysts.failure_test: Renewed depreciation materially weakens household real income or abrupt appreciation exposes FX-only earnings.

catalysts.name: Second-quarter GDP
catalysts.confirmation_test: Household consumption and business investment broaden domestic-demand growth.
catalysts.failure_test: Domestic demand contracts or growth depends mainly on inventories, fiscal transfers, or external demand.

opportunities.name: Financial normalization beneficiaries
independent_return_engines: Higher asset yields and net-interest income
opportunities.catalyst: Further orderly BOJ normalization with stable credit conditions.
opportunities.main_risk: Duration losses, funding-cost pressure, or credit deterioration offset the benefit of higher rates.
opportunities.next_action: Screen banks and insurers for deposit quality, asset sensitivity, duration exposure, credit risk, capital returns, and valuation; create company packets for qualifying names.

company_review.reason: No named company has been selected, and company-specific return engines, valuation requirements, and catalyst exposure have not been verified.

opportunities.name: Governance and capital-allocation reform beneficiaries
opportunities.catalyst: Implementation of the July 2026 Corporate Governance Code revision.
opportunities.main_risk: Governance compliance remains cosmetic and does not improve returns on capital.
opportunities.next_action: Identify companies showing completed capital-allocation actions and initiate valuation handoffs only after company-specific triggers are satisfied.

company_review.reason: The governance catalyst is material at the theme level, but no named company has yet demonstrated sufficient company-specific implementation and valuation need.

opportunities.name: Labor-saving, automation, and productivity investment
opportunities.catalyst: Business investment aimed at automation, digitalization, and labor substitution.
opportunities.main_risk: High input costs, project delays, or insufficient customer returns reduce investment demand.
opportunities.next_action: Build a candidate list with independently verified order growth, margins, recurring revenue, and domestic-demand exposure.

company_review.reason: No named company has been evaluated for independent return engines, valuation requirements, or company-specific catalysts.

opportunities.name: Quality exporters with proprietary pricing power
opportunities.catalyst: Continued external demand and evidence that local-currency margins and unit growth remain strong.
opportunities.main_risk: Reported profit growth is primarily currency translation while underlying demand or margins weaken.
opportunities.next_action: Remove FX translation from operating analysis and require a company valuation review before any security-level action.

company_review.reason: Theme evidence does not identify a specific exporter whose pricing power and independent return engines have been verified.

opportunities.name: Domestic services and consumption beneficiaries
opportunities.catalyst: Sustained positive real wages and broader household consumption.
opportunities.main_risk: Imported inflation and weak household sentiment prevent nominal wage gains from translating into real demand.
opportunities.next_action: Monitor real wages and household consumption before increasing conviction or initiating company reviews.

company_review.reason: The domestic-demand assumption remains mixed and no named company has sufficient evidence for promotion.

opportunities.name: Currency-hedged broad Japan exposure
independent_return_engines: Reduction of adverse yen translation for foreign investors
opportunities.catalyst: Broader sector participation and continuing governance reform.
opportunities.main_risk: Hedging costs reduce returns or yen appreciation makes unhedged exposure superior.
opportunities.next_action: Compare hedged and unhedged expected returns, implementation costs, and scenario sensitivity before selecting an instrument.

company_review.reason: This is a fund category rather than a named operating company.

risks.name: Persistent real-income deterioration
risks.trigger: Nominal wage growth repeatedly trails inflation and household consumption weakens.
risks.scenario_impact: Raises bear probability and lowers domestic-reflation opportunity rankings.

risks.name: Disorderly monetary normalization
risks.trigger: JGB volatility, funding costs, or credit stress rise sharply following policy tightening.
risks.scenario_impact: Weakens the thesis and can invalidate the financial-normalization opportunity.

risks.name: Imported-inflation regime
risks.trigger: Yen depreciation and commodity costs raise inflation without corresponding productivity or wage gains.
risks.scenario_impact: Reduces household demand and increases the probability that inflation is not a healthy reflation signal.

risks.name: Cosmetic governance compliance
risks.trigger: Disclosure and policy changes do not produce measurable capital returns, asset releases, or ROE improvement.
risks.scenario_impact: Lowers the ranking of governance-reform beneficiaries.

risks.name: Narrow market leadership
risks.trigger: Equity returns remain concentrated in a small number of exporters or AI-linked firms.
risks.scenario_impact: Reduces confidence that the structural opportunity is broadening.

risks.name: Global-demand shock
risks.trigger: External demand or global capital expenditure deteriorates materially.
risks.scenario_impact: Weakens exporters, business investment, and the fair scenario.

risks.name: Exporter false positives
risks.trigger: Profit growth is predominantly translation-driven while unit demand or local-currency margins deteriorate.
risks.scenario_impact: Requires exporter opportunity downgrades and company-level rejection.

next_decision_points.decision_test: Determine whether rebasing materially changes the assessment of inflation breadth and household purchasing-power pressure.

publication.headline: JPY Thesis Intact as Orderly Normalization and Governance Reform Offset Real-Income Risk
publication.summary: Japan's structural investment thesis remains intact. BOJ normalization and governance reform support financial and capital-allocation opportunities, while weak household purchasing power and imported inflation keep the fair scenario dominant.
